svg.aria-label: How to write 字: 6 strokes · 5 pen lifts · 9 movements
svg.title: Writing 字
svg.desc: 9 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 字 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 字.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E5%AD%97.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 字. Medians 1–3 draw 宀 first: a down-right top dot, a separately started left-side down-left stroke, and a separately started horizontal roof that hooks down-left without lifting. Medians 4–6 then draw 子: a top horizontal that turns down-left without lifting, a separately started vertical that hooks left without lifting, and a final middle horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, all three joined turns, and five intervening lifts; Noto's roof is wider and 子's vertical hook is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.
